meta.subtitle: From the 2013 MIT-founded fast-reactor startup through the May 2024 AltC SPAC business combination into the multi-gigawatt order book that has driven the equity narrative
meta.abstract: Oklo Inc. (OKLO, NYSE) is the Santa Clara-headquartered advanced nuclear reactor developer founded in 2013 by Jacob DeWitte and Caroline Cochran (both MIT-trained nuclear engineers) to commercialise a sodium-cooled fast-reactor design called the Aurora powerhouse. The company went public on May 10, 2024 through business combination with AltC Acquisition Corp, the SPAC sponsored by then-OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Altman had served as Chairman of Oklo before the SPAC transaction and continued as Chairman of the post-listing public company until April 2025, when he stepped down to focus on OpenAI specifically and avoid potential conflicts of interest as OpenAI's compute infrastructure increasingly required nuclear-scale electricity that Oklo's commercial roadmap might supply. DeWitte continues as Chief Executive Officer; Caroline Cochran as Chief Operating Officer; CFO Craig Bealmear joined to lead post-SPAC public-company finance functions. Oklo is structurally pre-commercial — the company has zero recurring revenue and operates as a research and development company funded through a combination of the SPAC-listing capital, subsequent equity issuances, and Department of Energy fuel and site partnerships. The product trajectory targets first commercial operation of the Aurora powerhouse at the Idaho National Laboratory site by 2027-2028, with subsequent commercial deployments at customer sites following. The order book has been characterised through quarterly disclosures and customer announcements as multi-gigawatt across data centre, US Air Force, and adjacent customer commitments; specific customer deals announced through 2024-2025 include Switch (the data centre operator), Equinix (the colocation operator), Diamondback Energy (the Permian Basin oil and gas producer), and the US Air Force base electricity supply programmes. FY2025 (calendar year 2025) operating loss was substantial, reflecting the R&D and development capex required to pursue the first commercial deployments; the balance sheet at the FY2025 close carried meaningful cash from equity issuances supporting multi-year forward runway. The investment proposition compresses regulatory approval execution at the NRC (the Aurora powerhouse design certification and combined license processes), commercial deployment execution (the 2027-2028 first commercial operation target requires substantial technical, regulatory, and operational milestones), the broader SMR and advanced reactor industry maturation through the late 2020s, and the AI data centre electricity demand sustaining at levels that justify the long-cycle commitments customers have made.

Oklo Inc. DeWitte continues as Chief Executive Officer; Caroline Cochran as Chief Operating Officer; CFO Craig Bealmear joined to lead post-SPAC public-company finance functions. chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
Oklo completed its business combination with AltC Acquisition Corp. on 9 May 2024 and began trading on the New York Stock Exchange under `OKLO` on 10 May 2024. The July 2023 merger announcement had set a pre-money equity value of $850 million for Legacy Oklo, while the closing delivered approximately $306 million of gross proceeds before transaction expenses to the public company. [Oklo merger announcement](https://www.oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2023/Oklo-an-Advanced-Fission-Technology-Company-to-Go-Public-via-Merger-with-AltC-Acquisition-Corp/default.aspx) [Oklo listing announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Inc.-Begins-Trading-on-the-New-York-Stock-Exchange/default.aspx)

## Founders and Technology

Oklo was founded in July 2013 by Jacob DeWitte and Caroline DeWitte, then Caroline Cochran. The distinction mattered: Oklo’s own 2026 proxy showed DeWitte as an MIT-trained nuclear engineer with a Ph.D. and S.M. in nuclear engineering, while Caroline DeWitte held an S.M. in nuclear engineering from MIT and undergraduate degrees in economics and mechanical engineering from the University of Oklahoma. [Oklo 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

The Aurora powerhouse was described in Oklo’s 2024 and 2025 SEC filings as a compact sodium-cooled fast reactor product line designed to produce 15 MWe to 75 MWe, with the company also discussing larger future configurations. The technology thesis rested on EBR-II heritage at Idaho National Laboratory and on Oklo’s plan to pair fast-spectrum reactors with fresh or recycled fuel. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

## Customer Pipeline

The commercial case crystallised through a sequence of non-binding customer commitments. A February 2024 letter of intent gave an unnamed third party later identified by market reporting as Equinix a 36-month right of first refusal on no less than 100 MWe and up to 500 MWe of output, in exchange for a $25 million payment made in March 2024. Oklo then announced a 100 MWe LOI with Wyoming Hyperscale on 23 May 2024 and a 50 MWe LOI with Diamondback Energy on 8 April 2024. By 13 November 2024, two additional data-centre LOIs for up to 750 MWe had lifted the disclosed customer pipeline to approximately 2,100 MWe. [Oklo Q1 2024 financial statements](https://oklo.com/files/doc_financials/2024/q1/oklo-q1-2024-financial-statements-filed-5-13-2024.pdf) [Wyoming Hyperscale LOI](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Partners-with-Wyoming-Hyperscale-to-Deliver-100-Megawatts-to-its-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Diamondback LOI](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Signs-LOI-to-Supply-50-Megawatts-of-Power-to-Diamondback-Energy/default.aspx) [750 MWe data-center LOIs](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Secures-Partnerships-for-Up-to-750-Megawatts-of-Power-for-U.S.-Data-Centers/)

The inflection came on 18 December 2024, when Oklo and Switch signed a non-binding Master Power Agreement covering 12 gigawatts of Aurora deployments through 2044. Oklo’s own 2024 annual report later said the December 2024 Switch agreement and the two additional 750 MWe LOIs took the order book to approximately 14,100 MWe. [Switch agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

On 9 January 2026, Oklo and Meta announced a separate agreement supporting a 1.2 GW power campus in Pike County, Ohio. Oklo said the arrangement created a mechanism for Meta to prepay for power and fund fuel procurement and Phase 1 development activity; the site covered 206 acres formerly owned by the Department of Energy, with first-phase service targeted as early as 2030 and the full 1.2 GW build-out targeted by 2034. [Oklo-Meta Ohio agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

## Financial Baseline

Oklo remained pre-revenue through the frozen window, but the balance sheet changed materially. Its 2024 Form 10-K put year-end cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities at $275.3 million; the 2025 Form 10-K put the same figure at $1.4125 billion after underwritten offerings and ATM issuance; and the 31 March 2026 Form 10-Q put it at $2.5369 billion. In the first quarter of 2026 alone, Oklo sold 12,376,352 shares under its ATM programme for gross proceeds of $1.1999 billion and net proceeds of $1.1819 billion. Q1 2026 net loss was $33.1 million and cash used in operating activities was $17.9 million. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## Licensing and Governance

The regulatory picture was more complicated than a simple NRC review clock. The NRC completed a pre-application readiness assessment for Phase 1 of a future combined licence application in July 2025 and accepted Oklo’s Principal Design Criteria topical report for accelerated review in September 2025. Oklo broke ground on Aurora-INL in September 2025 under the Department of Energy’s Reactor Pilot Program pathway, signed a DOE Other Transaction Agreement and received Nuclear Safety Design Agreement approval in March 2026, and then won NRC approval of the PDC topical report on 6 May 2026. Separately, the NRC’s Part 53 advanced-reactor rule was published on 30 March 2026 and became effective on 29 April 2026. [NRC readiness assessment](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Advances-Licensing-with-Completion-of-NRC-Readiness-Assessment/default.aspx) [PDC acceptance](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Accepted-for-Review-Under-an-Accelerated-Timeline/default.aspx) [Aurora-INL groundbreaking](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Breaks-Ground-on-First-Aurora-Powerhouse/default.aspx) [DOE OTA and NSDA](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [PDC approval](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Approved-for-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx) [Part 53 final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/03/30/2026-06048/risk-informed-technology-inclusive-regulatory-framework-for-advanced-reactors)

Governance shifted too. Sam Altman resigned as chair and director on 22 April 2025; Oklo’s 2026 proxy later recorded Jacob DeWitte, not John Jansen, as having served as chairman since April 2025. Jansen remained on the board as a retired U.S. Marine Corps lieutenant general. [Altman resignation 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925037472/tm2512904d1_8k.htm) [Oklo 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

## The Central Tension

By 23 May 2026, Oklo still traded on commitments, milestones and capital-market access rather than on electricity sales. Its first Idaho reactor had moved onto a DOE authorization pathway, while the company said it would subsequently pursue NRC licensing for commercial operations. The investment case therefore still compressed three linked tasks into one equity narrative: turning LOIs and framework agreements into binding PPAs, securing enough HALEU and fabrication capacity to support first deployments, and converting DOE-backed demonstration progress into a repeatable commercial licensing path. [DOE OTA and NSDA](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

chapters.title: From 2013 MIT founding to the AltC SPAC merger
chapters.body:
## The Founders and the Fast Reactor

Oklo’s origin story was narrower and more technical than the shorthand usually suggested. Jacob DeWitte and Caroline Cochran met in the Massachusetts Institute of Technology nuclear-science orbit, but they did not arrive with identical academic biographies. Oklo’s 2026 proxy identified DeWitte as an MIT Ph.D. candidate from January 2011 to June 2014, holding both a Ph.D. and an S.M. in nuclear engineering, while Caroline DeWitte held an S.M. in nuclear engineering from MIT and undergraduate degrees in economics and mechanical engineering from the University of Oklahoma. They incorporated Oklo in July 2013 and anchored it to a part of the American reactor canon the commercial industry had largely left behind: the sodium-cooled fast reactor. [Oklo 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

The design lineage ran back to Experimental Breeder Reactor-II at Idaho National Laboratory, a sodium-cooled metallic-fuel reactor that Oklo repeatedly cited as the proof that fast-reactor physics could deliver passive safety and efficient fuel use. Oklo’s own 2024 annual report described Aurora as an EBR-II-derived product line designed to produce 15 MWe to 75 MWe, with the potential to expand above that range over time. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

The Y Combinator admission in 2014 mattered less for capital than for signalling. It pulled a deep-nuclear engineering story into Silicon Valley’s growth ecosystem and helped establish the investor bridge that would later culminate in Sam Altman’s sponsorship. But the technical thesis remained stubbornly nuclear: metallic fuel, sodium coolant, compact plant size, and a business model built around selling electricity rather than selling reactor blueprints. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

## The NRC Application and the 2022 Denial

Oklo’s first serious regulatory leap came on 11 March 2020, when it submitted what the NRC described as the first combined licence application for an advanced non-light-water reactor in the agency’s history. The target was Aurora at Idaho National Laboratory. That filing was historically important and operationally premature. On 6 January 2022, the NRC denied the application without prejudice for failure to supply information on several key topics. The agency’s application page and documents table show that the denial sat alongside completeness determinations for Oklo’s maximum credible accident and performance-based licensing methodology topical reports, underscoring that the problem was not a one-line procedural miss but an information-completeness failure across core parts of the safety case. [NRC Aurora application page](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/new-reactors/large-lwr/col/aurora-oklo.html) [NRC Aurora documents table](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/new-reactors/large-lwr/col/aurora-oklo/documents.html) [NRC press release, 6 January 2022](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/news/2022/22-002.pdf)

That distinction mattered. The denial was not a substantive finding that the Aurora concept was unsafe; it was an official judgment that the submission did not provide enough information for the NRC to continue the review. The practical effect, however, was just as consequential as a slower-moving merits fight would have been. Oklo lost the simple narrative that it was already moving through a conventional NRC review queue and instead had to rebuild credibility through years of pre-application work, topical reports and narrower regulatory milestones. [NRC Aurora application page](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/new-reactors/large-lwr/col/aurora-oklo.html) [NRC Aurora documents table](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/new-reactors/large-lwr/col/aurora-oklo/documents.html)

Public disclosures after the denial did not support the claim that Oklo had refiled a new combined licence application in late 2023. What they showed instead was a slower reconstruction. In July 2025, Oklo said it had completed the NRC’s pre-application readiness assessment for Phase 1 of a future COLA, with the NRC identifying no significant gaps that would hinder acceptance. In September 2025, it said the NRC had accepted the Principal Design Criteria topical report for accelerated review. By March 2026, however, the company was describing Aurora-INL as moving ahead under the Department of Energy’s Reactor Pilot Program authorization pathway while it continued progressing its engagement for future NRC licensing for commercial operations. [NRC readiness assessment](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Advances-Licensing-with-Completion-of-NRC-Readiness-Assessment/default.aspx) [PDC acceptance](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Accepted-for-Review-Under-an-Accelerated-Timeline/default.aspx) [DOE OTA and NSDA](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx)

## Sam Altman, AltC, and the SPAC Transaction

The financial narrative changed on 11 July 2023, when Oklo announced a merger with AltC Acquisition Corp., the Sam Altman-sponsored SPAC. The announcement set a pre-money equity value of $850 million for Legacy Oklo and said the transaction could provide up to $500 million of gross capital, or as much as $516 million of cash on the balance sheet if AltC shareholders did not redeem and before transaction expenses. The framing was unapologetically forward-looking: Oklo had no revenue, no operating reactor and no NRC licence, but it did have a reactor story that sat squarely inside the emerging AI-power thesis. [Oklo merger announcement](https://www.oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2023/Oklo-an-Advanced-Fission-Technology-Company-to-Go-Public-via-Merger-with-AltC-Acquisition-Corp/default.aspx)

Altman’s relevance extended beyond branding. Oklo’s May 2024 listing announcement said he had been chairman since 2015 and quoted him not as a transient SPAC promoter but as a long-term insider backing the company’s public-market transition. That continuity amplified the market’s willingness to treat Oklo as a proxy for both advanced nuclear optionality and artificial-intelligence load growth. [Oklo listing announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Inc.-Begins-Trading-on-the-New-York-Stock-Exchange/default.aspx)

The closing happened on 9 May 2024, with public trading beginning the next day under `OKLO`. At closing, Oklo said it had received approximately $306 million of gross proceeds before expenses. That was materially below the no-redemption headline contemplated in 2023, but it was still enough to finance a much broader licensing, supply-chain and customer-development effort than the private company had previously been able to support. [Oklo listing announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Inc.-Begins-Trading-on-the-New-York-Stock-Exchange/default.aspx)

## Post-Merger Commercialisation and the Pipeline

Once listed, Oklo moved quickly to turn regulatory aspiration into commercial theatre. The Equinix arrangement, disclosed in 2024 financial statements, gave the counterparty a 36-month right of first refusal on 100 MWe to 500 MWe of output in exchange for a $25 million payment. It was followed by a 50 MWe LOI with Diamondback Energy and a 100 MWe LOI with Wyoming Hyperscale, later described in Oklo’s 2024 annual report as Prometheus Hyperscale, formerly Wyoming Hyperscale. [Oklo Q1 2024 financial statements](https://oklo.com/files/doc_financials/2024/q1/oklo-q1-2024-financial-statements-filed-5-13-2024.pdf) [Diamondback LOI](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Signs-LOI-to-Supply-50-Megawatts-of-Power-to-Diamondback-Energy/default.aspx) [Wyoming Hyperscale LOI](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Partners-with-Wyoming-Hyperscale-to-Deliver-100-Megawatts-to-its-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

The data-centre narrative then accelerated. On 13 November 2024, Oklo announced two additional LOIs for up to 750 MWe, bringing the disclosed pipeline to approximately 2,100 MWe. Five weeks later, Switch signed a non-binding 12 GW Master Power Agreement through 2044. In its 2024 annual report, Oklo said the disclosed order book had reached approximately 14,100 MWe. That was the commercial backdrop against which the stock increasingly traded: not on signed PPAs or delivered megawatt-hours, but on the scale and quality of counterparties willing to sign non-binding frameworks years before first power. [750 MWe data-center LOIs](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Secures-Partnerships-for-Up-to-750-Megawatts-of-Power-for-U.S.-Data-Centers/) [Switch agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

The federal story deepened too. In June 2025, Oklo said DLA Energy had issued a Notice of Intent to Award for the Eielson Air Force Base microreactor pilot, under which Oklo would design, construct, own and operate the plant and deliver electricity and heat under a long-term PPA. In January 2026, Meta separately agreed to support a 1.2 GW Ohio power campus through a prepayment structure tied to early procurement and development work. [Eielson NOITA](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selected-as-Intended-Awardee-to-Provide-Clean-Reliable-Power-to-Eielson-Air-Force-Base-in-Alaska/default.aspx) [Oklo-Meta Ohio agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

## The Board Transition

The governance transition was simpler than some secondary retellings implied. Sam Altman resigned as chair and director on 22 April 2025. Oklo’s 2026 proxy then recorded Jacob DeWitte as chairman from April 2025 onward. John Jansen remained a director, but he did not succeed Altman as chair. In the same period the board added Michael Thompson and Daniel Poneman, then in April 2026 added Mark Peters, David Christian, Derek Kan and David Park. [Altman resignation 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925037472/tm2512904d1_8k.htm) [Board additions, March 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925021750/tm258622d1_8k.htm) [Oklo 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

## Twelve Years and a Blank Income Statement

What the 2013-to-2026 arc had produced was unusual but more concrete than a pure-paper reactor dream. Oklo had become a listed company, raised large amounts of equity capital, built a multi-gigawatt book of non-binding demand, secured DOE site and fuel support, completed NRC readiness work and topical-report review milestones, and by September 2025 had broken ground on Aurora-INL. Yet it had still recognised no revenue, had not converted its headline customer frameworks into disclosed binding power-delivery contracts, and had not obtained an NRC operating licence for a commercial plant. [Aurora-INL groundbreaking](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Breaks-Ground-on-First-Aurora-Powerhouse/default.aspx) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

As of 23 May 2026, Oklo was therefore better described as a pre-revenue, early-construction, pre-commercial enterprise whose first Idaho reactor was advancing under DOE oversight while future commercial operations would still require NRC licensing. The market narrative had become real enough to command capital; the operating narrative still had to be built. [DOE OTA and NSDA](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

chapters.title: The Aurora powerhouse, fuel recycling, and the customer engagement model
chapters.body:
## The reactor at the core

The Aurora powerhouse sat at the centre of every Oklo business line. In Oklo’s own 2024 annual report, the company described Aurora as a fast-fission, sodium-cooled product family designed to produce 15 MWe to 75 MWe, with the potential to scale beyond that range. That mattered commercially because Oklo was not pitching a single gigawatt-class utility reactor; it was pitching a modular power plant small enough to fit remote industrial sites, military bases and individual data-centre campuses, but large enough to offer firm baseload power. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

## Heritage and passive safety: the EBR-II legacy

Oklo’s technical inheritance ran through Experimental Breeder Reactor-II, the sodium-cooled metallic-fuel reactor at Idaho National Laboratory that the Department of Energy highlighted as having operated from 1965 to 1994 and having demonstrated passive safety in landmark 1986 tests. That historical record was not a marketing flourish. It was the physical and regulatory lineage on which Oklo based Aurora’s claim to be a commercially packaged descendant of proven fast-reactor behaviour rather than a wholly untested concept. [DOE EBR-II overview](https://www.energy.gov/ne/articles/5-fast-facts-about-experimental-breeder-reactor-ii)

The 1986 passive-safety tests remained central to the argument. DOE’s summary of EBR-II recorded that operators deliberately cut power to the reactor’s cooling systems and let the machine shut itself down through its own feedback physics. Oklo’s case for Aurora inherited that logic: metallic fuel, sodium coolant, low operating pressure and negative reactivity feedback were meant to reduce reliance on active safety systems and to support an owner-operator power-sales model that would struggle under conventional large-reactor operating complexity. [DOE EBR-II overview](https://www.energy.gov/ne/articles/5-fast-facts-about-experimental-breeder-reactor-ii) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

## HALEU and the fuel-cycle distinction

Aurora’s fuel requirement set it apart from light-water SMRs and created one of the dossier’s most important supply-chain fault lines. DOE’s HALEU explainer defined high-assay low-enriched uranium as uranium enriched above the typical 5 percent ceiling for conventional reactor fuel and up to 19.75 percent uranium-235. Oklo’s filings consistently framed HALEU as necessary for Aurora’s compact core, long refuelling interval and fast-spectrum operating regime. [DOE HALEU overview](https://www.energy.gov/ne/nuclear-reactor-technologies/advanced-reactor-technologies/high-assay-low-enriched-uranium-haleu) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

The domestic supply base remained thin through the frozen window. Centrus’s Piketon cascade was the only NRC-licensed U.S. HALEU production line in operation, and by June 2025 the company said it had produced and delivered 900 kilograms of HALEU to DOE under Phase II of its contract, or more than 920 kilograms cumulatively including the initial 20-kilogram Phase I run. That was enough to prove process viability, not enough to underwrite fleet-scale deployment. [Centrus 900 kg milestone](https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/centrus-achieves-key-production-milestone-with-delivery-of-900-kilograms-of-haleu-to-the-department-of-energy/)

The supply challenge hardened in 2024. Congress made the Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act law on 13 May 2024, and DOE’s waiver guidance said the ban on Russian LEU imports took effect on 11 August 2024. DOE simultaneously began steering $2.7 billion toward domestic LEU and HALEU capability, but as of May 2026 the U.S. build-out remained a programme of contracts and expansions rather than a mature commercial market. [Congress.gov, Public Law 118-62](https://www.congress.gov/index.php/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/1042) [DOE waiver guidance](https://www.energy.gov/ne/russian-uranium-ban-waiver-guidance) [DOE $2.7 billion fuel-chain programme](https://www.energy.gov/articles/doe-announces-27-billion-president-bidens-investing-america-agenda-boost-domestic-nuclear)

Oklo’s partial answer was vertical integration. Its 2024 and 2025 disclosures described ambitions that stretched from HALEU procurement to fabrication and ultimately to recycling, with the company arguing that fast reactors could unlock value from used nuclear fuel that light-water reactors left behind. That was not yet a solved business. But it was a genuine business segment: powerhouses, fabrication, recycling and, by 2025, isotopes. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

## The owner-operator PPA model

Oklo’s commercial architecture differed sharply from the reactor-vendor template used by much of the nuclear industry. Its 2024 annual report said plainly that the company’s primary product would be energy produced by Aurora powerhouses and that it planned to sell that output through power purchase agreements rather than sell reactor designs. In other words, Oklo was trying to become an electricity producer with nuclear intellectual property, not merely an equipment vendor with licensing revenue. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

That structure moved the economic centre of gravity. If Oklo owned and operated the plants, then future upside sat in recurring power sales and project refinancing rather than in one-time reactor deliveries. The same structure also concentrated risk. Fuel procurement, construction execution, maintenance, insurance and nuclear-operating compliance would sit far more directly on Oklo’s balance sheet than under the conventional utility-owned model. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

## Customer pipeline and LOI structure

The pipeline was not static, and the timing mattered. By the time the SPAC merger closed in May 2024, Oklo had publicly disclosed a 500 MWe Equinix-style ROFR arrangement, a 50 MWe Diamondback LOI and a 100 MWe Wyoming Hyperscale LOI, or 650 MWe of specifically disclosed capacity. The later November 2024 data-centre LOIs added another 750 MWe and lifted the disclosed pipeline to roughly 2,100 MWe. [Oklo Q1 2024 financial statements](https://oklo.com/files/doc_financials/2024/q1/oklo-q1-2024-financial-statements-filed-5-13-2024.pdf) [Diamondback LOI](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Signs-LOI-to-Supply-50-Megawatts-of-Power-to-Diamondback-Energy/default.aspx) [Wyoming Hyperscale LOI](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Partners-with-Wyoming-Hyperscale-to-Deliver-100-Megawatts-to-its-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [750 MWe data-center LOIs](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Secures-Partnerships-for-Up-to-750-Megawatts-of-Power-for-U.S.-Data-Centers/)

Switch changed the scale of the discussion. Its December 2024 Master Power Agreement covered 12 GW through 2044. Oklo’s 2024 Form 10-K then described a total order book of approximately 14,100 MWe. That order book was not revenue, and it was not equivalent to signed PPAs. But it did define the company’s de facto segmentation: hyperscale data centres, remote industrial users, defence installations and, by 2026, dedicated data-centre campus development in Ohio. [Switch agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo-Meta Ohio agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

The Department of Defense pilot at Eielson Air Force Base sharpened the distributed-power thesis. Oklo’s June 2025 announcement said DLA Energy had issued a Notice of Intent to Award under which Oklo would design, construct, own and operate the plant and deliver electricity and heat to Eielson under a long-term PPA. Earlier DLA and Air Force materials had framed the Eielson pilot as the first military microreactor procurement, with the 2023 milestone describing a potential 30-year firm-fixed-price contract after licensing. [Oklo Eielson announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selected-as-Intended-Awardee-to-Provide-Clean-Reliable-Power-to-Eielson-Air-Force-Base-in-Alaska/default.aspx) [DLA micro-reactor milestone](https://www.dla.mil/About-DLA/News/News-Article-View/Article/3515062/micro-reactor-pilot-program-reaches-major-milestone/)

## The Idaho demonstration as the proving ground

Aurora-INL remained the hinge between theory and business. The first NRC route ended with the January 2022 denial. The later route was more layered: July 2025 readiness assessment for a future Phase 1 COLA, September 2025 PDC acceptance, September 2025 groundbreaking under the DOE Reactor Pilot Program, March 2026 DOE approval of the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement, and May 2026 NRC approval of the PDC topical report. [NRC readiness assessment](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Advances-Licensing-with-Completion-of-NRC-Readiness-Assessment/default.aspx) [PDC acceptance](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Accepted-for-Review-Under-an-Accelerated-Timeline/default.aspx) [Aurora-INL groundbreaking](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Breaks-Ground-on-First-Aurora-Powerhouse/default.aspx) [DOE OTA and NSDA](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [PDC approval](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Approved-for-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx)

The implication was subtle but critical. As of the frozen window, Aurora-INL was no longer best described as a reactor waiting inside a simple NRC combined-licence queue. It was a first deployment advancing under DOE authorization while Oklo continued building the NRC foundation for future commercial licensing. Every other business segment in the company, from customer contracting to fuel fabrication to recycling, still depended on that Idaho sequence working in practice rather than only in filings and presentations. [DOE OTA and NSDA](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

chapters.title: Pre-revenue economics, post-SPAC cash, and the LOI-to-revenue path
chapters.body:
## Post-SPAC Balance Sheet: The $306 Million Starting Line

Oklo’s entry into public markets was financially meaningful even if it was smaller than the headline no-redemption scenario sold at merger announcement. The July 2023 deal presentation valued Legacy Oklo at a pre-money equity value of $850 million and said the transaction could deliver up to $500 million of gross capital, or as much as $516 million of cash on the balance sheet assuming no redemptions and before expenses. What actually closed on 9 May 2024 was narrower: Oklo’s listing announcement said the company received approximately $306 million of gross proceeds before transaction expenses. [Oklo merger announcement](https://www.oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2023/Oklo-an-Advanced-Fission-Technology-Company-to-Go-Public-via-Merger-with-AltC-Acquisition-Corp/default.aspx) [Oklo listing announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Inc.-Begins-Trading-on-the-New-York-Stock-Exchange/default.aspx)

That distinction mattered because it set the initial financial perimeter of the public-company story. Oklo was not arriving in the market with construction financing in hand. It was arriving with enough cash to finance licensing work, staffing growth, supply-chain preparation and customer origination, while leaving the truly capital-intensive buildout phase for later rounds. The 2024 Form 10-K showed that as of 31 December 2024, after the first listed-company year, cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities stood at $275.3 million. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

## The Operating Loss Structure

The reported income statement was exactly what a pre-revenue reactor developer’s income statement should have looked like: losses dominated by engineering, regulatory and corporate-build costs rather than by cost of goods sold. For the year ended 31 December 2024, Oklo reported a net loss of $73.6 million, loss from operations of $52.8 million, and net cash used in operating activities of $38.4 million. For the year ended 31 December 2025, those figures widened to a net loss of $105.7 million, loss from operations of $139.3 million, and net cash used in operating activities of $82.2 million. In the first quarter of 2026, net loss was $33.1 million, loss from operations $51.2 million, and operating cash burn $17.9 million. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

The expense mix was also disclosed with unusual clarity. Oklo’s 2025 annual report attributed the year-on-year increase in general and administrative expense primarily to higher employee compensation and professional services, while the quarter-ended March 2026 filing showed research and development expense of $27.0 million and general and administrative expense of $24.2 million. This was not a business hiding plant-construction overruns inside opaque project accounting. It was a business visibly scaling payroll, consultants, licensing effort and early deployment activity. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## Cash Position and Runway: What the Filings Actually Said

The dossier’s earlier assumption of a simple sequential cash drawdown was not borne out by the filings. Oklo’s reported liquidity moved in two phases.

| Reporting date | Cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities | Filing language |
|---|---:|---|
| 31 Dec. 2024 | $275.3 million | Business-combination cash still defined the runway |
| 31 Mar. 2025 | $260.7 million | Liquidity modestly lower after one quarter of burn |
| 31 Dec. 2025 | $1.4125 billion | Equity issuance transformed the balance sheet |
| 31 Mar. 2026 | $2.5369 billion | ATM issuance expanded the war chest again |

[Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025025166/oklo-20250331.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

The critical correction was conceptual as much as numerical. Oklo did not tell investors that the original SPAC cash alone would fund operations “well into the late 2020s.” In each of the 2024 10-K, 2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q, management used a much narrower statement: the company believed its existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities were sufficient to fund operations for the one-year period following issuance of the financial statements. The cash buffer became much larger after 2025 and Q1 2026 equity issuance, but the company still did not present that as a self-contained solution to all construction-phase capital needs. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## Equity Capital Structure: Dilution Was the Mechanism

The balance-sheet expansion came from dilution. Oklo’s 2024 annual report showed 137,706,596 common shares outstanding at 31 December 2024. The 31 March 2026 Form 10-Q showed 173,867,839 shares outstanding at quarter-end, and 173,990,987 shares outstanding as of 7 May 2026. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

The 2025 financing sequence was especially important. Oklo’s 2025 annual report said net proceeds from underwritten public offerings and ATM programmes totalled $1.2636 billion during the year. It further broke out 10,781,891 shares sold through ATM programmes during 2025 for $822.0 million of net proceeds, plus a June 2025 underwritten common-stock offering that generated $440.1 million of net proceeds. Then in the first quarter of 2026, the company sold another 12,376,352 shares under the 2025 ATM programme at an average net price of $96.95 per share, generating $1.1819 billion of net proceeds. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

This was the financial truth beneath the stock’s momentum narrative. The market was willing to capitalise the company repeatedly at rising prices, and management used that window aggressively.

## The LOI Pipeline and the Revenue Gap

The customer stack was commercially meaningful, but the filings remained explicit that it was not yet revenue. Oklo’s 2024 annual report said the company had not yet constructed any powerhouses or entered into any binding contract with any customer to operate a plant or deliver electricity or heat. The same filing said its business plan was subject to converting non-binding instruments into binding agreements and that delays there could significantly delay revenue. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

That language sharpened the economic reality behind the headline order book. A 500 MWe ROFR arrangement, a 12 GW Switch master agreement and a 1.2 GW Ohio development plan with Meta all mattered because they reduced demand uncertainty. None of them, as of the frozen window, had turned Oklo into a company with contracted plant-level operating cash flow. [Oklo Q1 2024 financial statements](https://oklo.com/files/doc_financials/2024/q1/oklo-q1-2024-financial-statements-filed-5-13-2024.pdf) [Switch agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx) [Oklo-Meta Ohio agreement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm)

## Capital Allocation in the Pre-Revenue Phase

The use of cash followed directly from the business model. Oklo’s 2025 annual report said it expected significant ongoing expenditures to develop powerhouses, acquire fuel, develop fuel-fabrication and recycling facilities, and expand radioisotopes. The Q1 2026 10-Q made that shift even plainer: management said existing liquidity would fund powerhouses, radioisotopes and fuel businesses, operations and growth plans. That was a broader scope than the earlier private-company framing. The company was using public equity not only to keep the reactor effort alive but to assemble adjacent nuclear-fuel and isotope businesses around it. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

Capital expenditure was no longer negligible by early 2026. The first-quarter filing showed $32.8 million of property, plant and equipment purchases in the period and said the increase in investing cash use was driven partly by capital expenditures related to deployment of planned facilities. That was a meaningful change from the earlier stage in which the cash story had been almost entirely payroll, outside counsel and licensing documentation. [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## The Forward Capital Question

The forward capital question therefore did not disappear just because the cash balance exploded higher. It changed shape. By March 2026, Oklo had enough liquidity to move much faster on engineering, fuel, site work and adjacent nuclear businesses than it could have in May 2024. But the company’s own filings still warned that additional funding might be needed and that the amount of time and capital required to bring its powerhouses, recycling facilities and fuel-fabrication facilities to market could exceed expectations. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

In other words, the financial deep dive did not resolve into a simple bull case about cash runway. It resolved into a more precise proposition: Oklo had used a strong stock to buy time, engineering capacity and optionality. It still had to turn that optionality into licensed, financed and operating assets.

chapters.title: Post-SPAC quarterly cadence and the customer pipeline updates
chapters.body:
## The First Earnings Call: Q2 2024

Oklo's first public-company earnings cycle began only weeks after the AltC transaction closed on 9 May 2024 and the shares started trading on the New York Stock Exchange on 10 May. Management's initial task was less to explain revenue than to explain sequencing: the company had raised development capital, had no commercial sales, and was trying to persuade investors that regulatory progress, customer demand and fuel-chain preparation would move in a sufficiently coordinated fashion to turn a pre-revenue reactor developer into a long-duration power producer. [Oklo listing announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Inc.-Begins-Trading-on-the-New-York-Stock-Exchange/default.aspx) [Oklo Q2 2024 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000141057824001386/oklo-20240630x10q.htm)

That first quarter as a listed company did not support the simpler narrative that later crept into some market commentary: a one-time SPAC cash infusion followed by a steady burn-down toward a licensing verdict. The SEC record showed a more jagged capital story. Oklo finished June 2024 with roughly $294.6 million of cash and marketable debt securities, September 2024 with about $288.5 million, year-end 2024 with $275.3 million, and 31 March 2025 with $260.7 million. But from that point the balance sheet expanded rather than contracted: $683.0 million at 30 June 2025, $1.184 billion at 30 September 2025, $1.413 billion at 31 December 2025, and $2.537 billion at 31 March 2026, reflecting equity issuance rather than operating cash generation. [Oklo Q2 2024 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000141057824001386/oklo-20240630x10q.htm) [Oklo Q3 2024 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828024047875/oklo-20240930.htm) [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025025166/oklo-20250331.htm) [Oklo Q2 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025039571/oklo-20250630.htm) [Oklo Q3 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025051349/oklo-20250930.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## Cash and Operating Losses: The Balance Sheet Was Rebuilt, Not Merely Consumed

The operating profile remained recognisably pre-commercial. Net cash used in operating activities was $38.4 million for 2024, $82.2 million for 2025 and $17.9 million in the first quarter of 2026, while net loss was $73.6 million in 2024 and $105.7 million in 2025. What changed was not the absence of revenue but the company's willingness and ability to refill the war chest as the market re-rated nuclear names tied to the artificial-intelligence power theme. Oklo disclosed net proceeds of about $440.1 million from its June 2025 underwritten common-stock offering, then reported that it had sold 10.8 million shares through its at-the-market programme in 2025 for roughly $822.0 million of net proceeds, followed by another 12.4 million shares in the first quarter of 2026 for approximately $1.182 billion of net proceeds. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

| Period | Cash plus marketable debt securities | Primary financial inflection |
|---|---|---|
| June 30, 2024 | ~$294.6M | First post-listing quarter; SPAC proceeds still dominant |
| September 30, 2024 | ~$288.5M | Modest burn against expanding commercial outreach |
| December 31, 2024 | $275.3M | Year-end balance before renewed capital raising |
| March 31, 2025 | $260.7M | Pre-follow-on trough; one-year liquidity language remained standard |
| June 30, 2025 | $683.0M | Step-up after June underwritten equity offering |
| September 30, 2025 | $1.184B | ATM issuance materially enlarged the cash base |
| December 31, 2025 | $1.413B | Year-end capital position reset higher again |
| March 31, 2026 | $2.537B | Q1 2026 ATM issuance created another balance-sheet step-change |

The practical implication was important. Oklo's quarterly filings did not say the May 2024 close had funded the company "well into the late 2020s" on its own. They said, in the standard going-concern formulation, that existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities were expected to fund operations for at least one year from issuance of the financial statements. That was a narrower statement, and it was repeated even after the balance sheet had swelled with new equity. [Oklo Q1 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025025166/oklo-20250331.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## The Customer Pipeline Across Quarters

The quarterly investor script nonetheless remained demand-led. Management leaned on the build-own-operate model and the order book, not on near-term accounting revenue, to explain why a company with nil recognised sales could be discussed alongside infrastructure developers rather than speculative research ventures. By August 2024 Oklo said customer engagement exceeded 1,300 megawatts in non-binding letters of intent; by November 2024 it announced two additional data-centre partnerships for up to 750 MWe; and by the June 2025 quarter it said those agreements, together with previously disclosed commitments, could bring the Aurora order book to roughly 14,100 MWe. [Oklo-Siemens preferred supplier announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Establishes-Preferred-Supplier-Agreement-for-Steam-Turbine-Generator-Products-and-Services/default.aspx) [Oklo 750 MWe data-center announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Secures-Partnerships-for-Up-to-750-Megawatts-of-Power-for-U.S.-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Oklo Q2 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025039571/oklo-20250630.htm)

That order-book framing also explains why the company kept foregrounding named counterparties even though the commercial instruments remained mostly non-binding. The February 2024 Equinix letter of intent, the April 2024 Diamondback LOI, the May 2024 Wyoming Hyperscale LOI, the December 2024 Switch master agreement, the June 2025 Eielson intended award, and the January 2026 Meta agreement all mattered because they established queue position and strategic relevance in power-hungry customer segments. But the filings also remained careful: as of the 2025 annual report, Oklo still said it had not yet constructed any powerhouses or entered into any binding power purchase agreement with a customer to operate a plant or deliver electricity or heat. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo-Meta announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

## The Altman Departure and the April 2025 Governance Shift

The most visible governance event in the earnings window was not a financing but Sam Altman's resignation as chair and director, effective 22 April 2025. The company said the departure was not the result of a disagreement with Oklo. The succession was also more founder-centric than some summaries later suggested: the chair did not pass to John Jansen. Oklo's 2026 proxy said Jacob DeWitte had served as Chairman of the Board since April 2025, combining the chairmanship and the chief executive role. [Oklo 8-K, April 22 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925037472/tm2512904d1_8k.htm) [Oklo 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

That mattered because the equity had come to embody more than a standard nuclear-development story. The market was assigning option value not only to Aurora itself but also to Oklo's position in the AI-adjacent scramble for firm power. Altman's exit tested whether that premium could survive without the most famous technology name on the board. The answer, through the frozen window, was that the company compensated not with lower-risk fundamentals but with faster capital formation, more customer announcements and a visibly accelerated federal-development pathway.

## From "Updated COLA" to DOE Pilot Pathway

The regulatory narrative in the quarterly record also evolved. In the 2024 filings, Oklo still described itself as working toward an updated combined licence application after the NRC's 2022 denial without prejudice. By 2025, the company was disclosing a pre-application readiness assessment for its next COLA. But the critical change inside the frozen window came from outside the old "resubmitted COLA under review" frame: in August 2025 Oklo was selected for three Department of Energy Reactor Pilot Program projects; in September 2025 it broke ground on Aurora-INL; in March 2026 it announced DOE approval of the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement and the related Other Transaction Agreement for Aurora-INL; and in May 2026 it announced NRC approval of the principal design criteria topical report. As of 23 May 2026, the operative story was therefore a hybrid one of DOE-led authorisation for Aurora-INL, parallel NRC topical-report work and stated plans to pursue subsequent NRC licensing for commercial operations, not an already-docketed NRC merits review of a live combined-licence application. [Oklo Q1 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025025166/oklo-20250331.htm) [Oklo Reactor Pilot Program selection](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selected-for-Three-Projects-Under-U-S--Department-of-Energys-Reactor-Pilot-Program/default.aspx) [Oklo groundbreaking announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Breaks-Ground-on-First-Aurora-Powerhouse/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo NRC PDC approval announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Approved-for-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx)

By the frozen-window date, the earnings story therefore resolved into something more precise than the usual pre-revenue-growth-company template. Oklo had remained loss-making and operating-cash-negative; it had not yet booked reactor revenue; its customer queue still consisted largely of non-binding instruments. But it had also shown that the market was willing to refinance that gap repeatedly, that counterparties were willing to keep signing queue-position agreements, and that the federal-development pathway had shifted from a single-thread NRC review narrative to a broader DOE-and-NRC authorisation sequence. That was the real quarterly cadence investors were marking to market.

chapters.title: DeWitte, Cochran, Altman, and the technical-and-investor board
chapters.body:
## The Founders at the Helm

The most enduring fact about Oklo's leadership structure is also the simplest: the two people who filed the first paperwork to incorporate the company in 2013 remained its chief executive and chief operating officer at the time of the company's May 2024 New York Stock Exchange debut and through the frozen-window date of May 23, 2026. That continuity — Jacob DeWitte as CEO and Caroline DeWitte (née Cochran) as COO, in the same functional roles they had occupied since the company's formation — is unusual for a deep-technology startup that spent more than a decade in pre-revenue development, survived a Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing rejection, executed a SPAC transaction, and built a customer pipeline anchored by some of the largest data-centre operators in the United States. It is also, to sophisticated investors, one of the more legible risk signals the company offers: mission-aligned founder leadership with domain expertise in exactly the technical and regulatory problem that is Oklo's principal challenge.

## Jacob DeWitte: Engineer, Founder, Chairman

Jacob DeWitte turned 40 in the year the 2026 annual meeting proxy was filed. He completed a B.S. in Nuclear Engineering at the University of Florida and a Ph.D. at MIT's Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering (2011–2014), founding Oklo in July 2013 during his doctoral candidacy.

The technical biography runs deeper still. Over a dozen years before founding Oklo, DeWitte served as an intern or fellow at Sandia National Laboratories during the summers of 2002, 2003, 2006, and 2007; at Urenco Limited, the uranium enrichment supplier, in 2005; as a research intern at General Electric in 2008; and as a Visiting Fellow at the United States Naval Nuclear Laboratory in 2009 and 2011. He sat on the board of the American Nuclear Society from 2009 to 2011. By the time he filed Oklo's incorporation documents, DeWitte had accumulated roughly a decade of hands-on exposure across enrichment, utility-scale reactor services, national-laboratory research, and naval nuclear applications — a span that is atypical for founders in the advanced reactor space.

The corporate governance role evolved materially during the twelve months before the snapshot date. Altman's departure from the board on April 22, 2025 left the chairmanship vacant. The board named DeWitte to fill it: per the 2026 annual meeting proxy statement filed with the SEC on April 21, 2026, DeWitte has served as Chairman of the Board since April 2025, combining the chairman and chief executive roles in a single seat. [Oklo Inc. DEF 14A, April 21, 2026, SEC EDGAR CIK 0001849056](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

## Caroline DeWitte: Co-Founder, COO, and Nuclear Engineer

Caroline DeWitte, who was known professionally as Caroline Cochran through Oklo's pre-public period, co-founded the company alongside Jacob DeWitte at Oklo's inception in July 2013. The pair are married to each other, a fact disclosed in both the 2025 and 2026 proxy statements. The co-founder partnership has been a continuous structural feature of the company across its entire operating history.

Her educational profile differs from her co-founder's in a notable way that is often glossed over in shorthand references to Oklo's "two MIT nuclear engineers." DeWitte holds a Master of Science in Nuclear Engineering from MIT — she studied there from 2007 to 2010 — but her undergraduate degrees are a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Oklahoma, where she later received the Regent's Outstanding Alumni Award. Before founding Oklo, she worked as a marketing and engineering consultant from March 2011 to July 2013 and carried policy exposure from a Programs Analysis and Evaluation internship at the Office of the Secretary of Defense in 2005. From 2018 to 2019 she served on the U.S. Department of Energy's Nuclear Energy Advisory Committee and appeared as a panel member at the ninth Clean Energy Ministerial. [Oklo Inc. DEF 14A, April 21, 2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

The COO scope across Oklo's pre-commercial period spans customer pipeline management, operational execution, and the regulatory-interface work that runs alongside NRC licensing. As a board director since May 2024, Caroline DeWitte is among the Class II directors standing for re-election at the June 2026 annual meeting.

## The Executive Tier

Beneath the co-founder pair, the executive team was substantially restructured for the public-company phase. R. Craig Bealmear, 59, joined as Chief Financial Officer of Legacy Oklo in August 2023 — roughly nine months before the SPAC merger closed — and has continued in that role post-listing. His prior career was heavily concentrated in hydrocarbon energy finance: he served as Chief Financial Officer of Renewable Energy Group, a biodiesel producer acquired by Chevron Corporation in June 2022, from April 2021 to December 2022; before that, as Chief Financial Officer for North America Downstream at BP plc from March 2015 to December 2020; and before that as Deputy Chief Financial Officer for BP's Refining and Marketing segment from January 2013. The full BP and Atlantic Richfield tenure spanned 28 years. Bealmear holds an M.B.A. from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania and serves on the board of trustees of Bellarmine University. His arrival in mid-2023 signalled the company's deliberate preparation for SEC reporting obligations and public-market investor relations ahead of the AltC combination.

William Goodwin, 41, joined as Chief Legal and Strategy Officer in August 2024, three months after the listing. Goodwin brought aviation and mobility regulatory experience: he had served as Deputy General Counsel and in special projects and strategy roles at Joby Aviation, the electric air-taxi developer; as Head of Policy, Regulatory, and Legal at Skyryse; and as General Counsel and Vice President of Policy at AirMap. His JD is from UCLA School of Law; he holds an M.A. in Political Philosophy from Claremont Graduate University and a B.A. in Classics from the University of Southern California. The combination of aviation regulatory experience and strategy responsibility made him, in effect, the company's interface between NRC process management and the broader strategic function. [Oklo Inc. DEF 14A, April 21, 2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

## The Altman Connection: Sponsorship and Its Limits

Sam Altman was an early-stage investor in Legacy Oklo before backing AltC Acquisition Corp, the SPAC that merged with Oklo in May 2024. Michael Klein's M. Klein and Company served as the organising sponsor. Altman became Chairman immediately post-merger.

The chairmanship lasted eleven months. On April 22, 2025, Altman filed notification with the Oklo board of his intention to resign as Chair and as a Class II director, effective that same day. The 8-K filed simultaneously stated that "Mr. Altman's decision to resign was not due to any disagreement with the Company on any matter related to the Company's operations, policies or practices." [Oklo Inc. Form 8-K, April 22, 2025, SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925037472/tm2512904d1_8k.htm) Altman's departure was complete — not a transition to a lesser board role — and coincided with the period in which OpenAI's infrastructure ambitions were creating increasingly visible tension with any concurrent Oklo board seat: as Oklo's commercial pipeline deepened into data-centre electricity supply contracts with exactly the operators serving AI compute workloads, the conflict-of-interest optics had become difficult to manage.

His departure removed the highest-profile governance signal Oklo had possessed since the listing, and the share price registered the event. The board's response — naming the sitting CEO as Chairman rather than appointing an external successor — was a deliberate choice to consolidate governance authority in DeWitte rather than seek a replacement anchor sponsor from outside.

## Board Reconstruction: Depth Through Transition

The board that existed at the frozen-window date of May 23, 2026 was materially different from the post-SPAC roster of twelve months prior. Eleven directors occupied three staggered classes.

Two additions in March 2025 added substantive policy and nuclear-industry depth. Daniel B. Poneman, 70, former Deputy Secretary of Energy under President Obama from 2009 to 2014 and subsequently President and CEO of Centrus Energy Corp from 2015 to 2023 — where he oversaw the launch of the first US-technology-enabled domestic uranium enrichment production since 1954 — joined as a Class III director. His enrichment-industry background is directly relevant to Oklo's HALEU fuel dependencies. Michael Thompson, 49, Managing Partner of Reinvent Capital, a technology-focused private investment fund, joined alongside Poneman. [Oklo Inc. Form 8-K, March 4, 2025, SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925021750/tm258622d1_8k.htm)

April 2026 brought three further additions: Derek Kan, former Deputy Director of the White House Office of Management and Budget and Under Secretary for Policy at the Department of Transportation, currently Vice Chairman of the U.S. Postal Service Board of Governors; David Park, CEO of Standard Lithium (NYSE: SLI) and a former Koch Strategic Platforms president with early-career nuclear exposure at Atomic Energy of Canada; and Dr. Mark Peters, former Director of Idaho National Laboratory and former Executive Vice President at Battelle Memorial Institute — whose Idaho National Laboratory affiliation is specifically relevant given Oklo's site agreement with INL for the Aurora demonstration plant. David A. Christian, former Chief Nuclear Officer and Chief Innovation Officer of Dominion Energy, joined the same month, adding operational nuclear experience from one of the largest US nuclear operators. [Oklo Inc. DEF 14A, April 21, 2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

The Class I roster retained Michael Klein, who has served continuously since AltC's formation, and Lt. Gen. (ret.) John Jansen of the United States Marine Corps — where Jansen culminated a career as Deputy Commandant for Programs and Resources and also held the role of Chairman of the Board of Directors of Marine Corps Community Services, retiring in October 2021 after nearly four decades that included duty as a carrier pilot, TOPGUN graduate, and multiple commands. One earlier departure is also relevant context: Christopher Wright, then CEO of Liberty Energy, had served on Oklo's board through 2024 before resigning on January 13, 2025, effective upon his Senate confirmation as U.S. Secretary of Energy. [Oklo Inc. Form 8-K, January 13, 2025, SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925004527/tm253619d1_8k.htm) Wright's confirmation elevated a sitting Oklo board member into the Cabinet position with jurisdiction over advanced-reactor demonstration funding and the HALEU supply chain — an unusual alignment, though one the company had no formal mechanism to exploit after his departure from the board.

Richard W. Kinzley, former Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Black Hills Corporation, a multi-state electric utility, rounds out the audit-focused independent directors, having served since the May 2024 merger date.

The full eleven-member board — anchored by the co-founder executive pair, reinforced with a former DOE deputy secretary, a former INL director, a former Dominion nuclear chief, and a Marine Corps lieutenant general — reflects the specific requirements of a pre-commercial advanced-reactor developer: technical credibility for the NRC licensing process, policy fluency for DOE and DOD customer relationships, and financial oversight adequate for a public company burning cash against a long-dated commercial horizon.

chapters.title: Equinix, Switch, hyperscalers, DoD, and the HALEU supply
chapters.body:
## The Equinix Anchor: A Paid Queue Position on up to 500 MWe

The customer relationship that most clearly signalled outside willingness to finance Oklo's commercial queue was the February 2024 letter of intent with Equinix. Oklo's SEC filings identified the counterparty by name and set out unusually specific economics for what was still a non-binding framework: the LOI was executed on 16 February 2024; it contemplated future power purchase agreements serving Equinix data centres in the United States over a 20-year horizon; it granted Equinix a continuing right of first refusal for 36 months on no less than 100 MWe and up to 500 MWe of output from covered US powerhouses; and, in exchange for those rights and related protections, Equinix paid Oklo $25 million in March 2024. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2024 S-1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465924073383/oklo-20240331xs1.htm) [Equinix LOI exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465924047344/tm2324337d21_ex10-19.htm)

That mattered because the $25 million was not a small symbolic reservation fee. It amounted to a real cash transfer from an investment-grade data-centre operator to a reactor developer that had not yet built a plant. The transaction did not solve Oklo's financing problem, but it did establish that a sophisticated infrastructure buyer was prepared to spend money to secure optionality in a market where dispatchable carbon-free power had begun to look structurally scarce.

## From 1.3 GW to 14.1 GW: The Data-Centre Queue Expanded Fast

The Equinix arrangement did not remain an isolated customer curiosity. On 23 May 2024, Oklo said it had signed a non-binding LOI with Wyoming Hyperscale to collaborate on a 20-year PPA for 100 megawatts of clean power for a data-centre campus. On 13 November 2024, it announced two additional non-binding data-centre partnerships for up to 750 MWe combined. Then, on 18 December 2024, Oklo and Switch signed a non-binding master power agreement to deploy 12 gigawatts of Aurora projects through 2044, one of the largest corporate clean-power agreements announced anywhere in the sector. By the June 2025 quarter, Oklo said the data-centre and related commercial queue could bring its order book to roughly 14,100 MWe. [Wyoming Hyperscale announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Partners-with-Wyoming-Hyperscale-to-Deliver-100-Megawatts-to-its-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [750 MWe data-center announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Secures-Partnerships-for-Up-to-750-Megawatts-of-Power-for-U.S.-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Switch master agreement announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx) [Oklo Q2 2025 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025039571/oklo-20250630.htm)

The order of magnitude was striking, but so was the legal caveat. Switch's 12 GW agreement was explicitly a framework under which individual binding agreements were expected to be finalised as project milestones were reached. The same qualifier ran through the rest of the customer book. The commercial value lay in demonstrated demand and site prioritisation, not in already-contracted reactor cash flow.

The queue continued to widen inside the frozen window. On 17 January 2025, Oklo said it had signed a memorandum of understanding with RPower to pair immediately deployable gas generation with a later transition to Aurora power. On 23 July 2025, it announced a similar integrated-power alliance with Liberty Energy, and Liberty noted that it had committed $10 million to Oklo in 2023 as an early investor. On 27 January 2026, Oklo and Meta announced an agreement supporting up to 1.2 GW of nuclear-energy development in southern Ohio, including a mechanism for prepayment and development funding. Those arrangements did not convert the queue into recognised revenue, but they did show that Oklo's customer universe had broadened from pure data-centre off-take to multi-stage infrastructure collaborations. [Oklo-RPower announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-and-RPower-Join-Forces-to-Accelerate-Power-Availability-for-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Oklo-Liberty announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-and-Liberty-Energy-Launch-Next-Generation-Integrated-Power-Solution/default.aspx) [Oklo-Meta announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

## Industrial Load and the Defence Customer

Oklo also pursued off-grid and defence-adjacent customers whose needs differed from the hyperscaler load-growth story. On 8 April 2024, it announced a non-binding LOI with Diamondback E&P LLC to supply 50 megawatts of power under a 20-year PPA for Permian Basin operations, with options to renew for additional 20-year terms. That was a cleaner statement of the industrial thesis than generic commentary about oil-and-gas interest in nuclear: Oklo was marketing small, behind-the-meter nuclear capacity to a customer with remote load and resilience needs rather than trying to sell a central-station plant into a regulated utility resource plan. [Diamondback LOI announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Signs-LOI-to-Supply-50-Megawatts-of-Power-to-Diamondback-Energy/default.aspx)

The Department of Defense lane was more procedurally significant. The Air Force and DLA Energy first announced in September 2023 that Oklo had received a notice of intent to award for the Eielson Air Force Base microreactor pilot, under which the company would have the opportunity to design, construct, own and operate a plant delivering power and heat under a long-term PPA. On 11 June 2025 Oklo said DLA Energy had again issued a NOITA, designating Oklo as the apparent successful offeror for the preferred installation at Eielson. The Air Force and DLA described the programme as a potential 30-year firm-fixed-price contract subject to successful NRC licensing, while Oklo described the later stage as a long-term power purchase agreement for electricity and heat at Eielson. [DLA Energy / Air Force announcement](https://www.dla.mil/About-DLA/News/News-Article-View/Article/3515062/micro-reactor-pilot-program-reaches-major-milestone/) [Oklo Eielson 2023 announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2023/Oklo-Tentatively-Selected-to-Provide-Clean-and-Resilient-Power-to-Eielson-Air-Force-Base/default.aspx) [Oklo Eielson 2025 announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selected-as-Intended-Awardee-to-Provide-Clean-Reliable-Power-to-Eielson-Air-Force-Base-in-Alaska/default.aspx)

## The Commercial Caveat: Still No Binding PPA by the Frozen Date

For all that commercial progress, the SEC language remained disciplined. Oklo's 2025 annual report said the company had not yet constructed any powerhouses or entered into any binding power purchase agreement with any customer to operate a plant or deliver electricity or heat. The same filing and the March 2026 quarterly report continued to describe Equinix, Diamondback and Prometheus Hyperscale as non-binding counterparties, even as the company said it was negotiating term sheets and binding PPAs with customers that had first signed letters of intent. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

That was the right way to read the customer book. It was neither a mirage nor bankable contracted revenue. It was a queue of counterparties, some of them unusually credible, whose willingness to wait still depended on regulatory timing, fuel availability, project economics and site execution.

## Supply Chain: Power Conversion, Construction and Fuel

The physical supply chain developed in parallel with the customer queue. In August 2024 Oklo named Siemens Energy as a preferred supplier for the Aurora power conversion system and said customer engagement already exceeded 1,300 megawatts in non-binding LOIs. In July 2025 it named Kiewit as lead constructor for Aurora-INL, with support spanning design, procurement and construction. Those announcements were not mere vendor name-drops: they showed Oklo moving from concept-market fit toward actual equipment and EPC sequencing for a first plant. [Oklo-Siemens preferred supplier announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Establishes-Preferred-Supplier-Agreement-for-Steam-Turbine-Generator-Products-and-Services/default.aspx) [Oklo-Kiewit announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selects-Kiewit-as-the-Lead-Constructor-for-First-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx)

Fuel remained the harder constraint. Aurora required HALEU, and the legal and industrial setting changed materially inside the window.
