President Biden signed the Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act on 13 May 2024, while DOE later issued waiver guidance describing the temporary exceptions process and, in December 2024, announced up to $2.7 billion in awards to expand domestic LEU and HALEU enrichment. Oklo's own fuel relationship with Centrus dated to August 2023, when the two companies signed an MOU covering fuel components and potential power procurement in southern Ohio. In June 2025 Centrus said it had delivered 900 kilograms of HALEU to DOE from the Piketon cascade, a meaningful technical milestone but still a small quantity relative to the needs implied by Oklo's longer-dated order book. [Congress.gov: H.R. 1042](https://www.congress.gov/index.php/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/1042) [DOE Russian uranium waiver guidance](https://www.energy.gov/ne/russian-uranium-ban-waiver-guidance) [DOE enrichment awards announcement](https://www.energy.gov/articles/doe-announces-27-billion-president-bidens-investing-america-agenda-boost-domestic-nuclear) [Oklo-Centrus announcement](https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/oklo-and-centrus-energy-sign-memorandum-of-understanding-for-fuel-components-and-power-procurement-to-support-the-deployment-of-advanced-fission-technologies-in-southern-ohio/) [Centrus 900 kg milestone](https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/centrus-achieves-key-production-milestone-with-delivery-of-900-kilograms-of-haleu-to-the-department-of-energy/)

Oklo's partial hedge was that it was not relying solely on future commercial enrichment output. The company had been awarded recovered EBR-II fuel material by DOE in 2019, had completed end-to-end recycling demonstrations, and by March 2026 had secured DOE approval of the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement for Aurora-INL alongside the DOE path for its co-located fuel-fabrication effort. The company said Aurora-INL was advancing under DOE's Reactor Pilot Program authorisation pathway and that it would subsequently pursue NRC licensing to support commercial operations. That sequence was more concrete than the older generic formulation that the fuel question was merely "under study", but it still left scaled fleet deployment dependent on domestic HALEU expansion. [DOE EBR-II background](https://www.energy.gov/ne/articles/5-fast-facts-about-experimental-breeder-reactor-ii) [Oklo recycling demonstration announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Completes-Successful-End-to-End-Demonstration-of-Advanced-Fuel-Recycling-Process/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx)

The net result was a supply chain that had become recognisable rather than theoretical. Counterparties, constructors, turbine suppliers and fuel partners were all on the board by the frozen date. None, however, removed the central truth of the investment case: the first plant still had to be licensed, fuelled, built and run before those relationships could mature into steady electricity revenue.

chapters.title: Where Oklo sits against NuScale, X-energy, TerraPower, Kairos, BWXT
chapters.body:
## The Listed Cohort

By the frozen-window date, the quoted US universe for advanced-reactor exposure was still thin, but it was not homogeneous. Oklo and NuScale were the clearest public-market pure plays. BWX Technologies was something different: a profitable, diversified nuclear contractor whose naval-reactor work remained the core of the business even as it pushed transportable microreactor and advanced-fuel programmes. Treating all three as interchangeable "SMR stocks" obscured the real distinction between a pre-revenue developer, a design-licensing company with a more mature light-water pathway, and an established contractor monetising advanced-reactor capabilities from an existing defence-industrial base. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [NuScale NRC US460 page](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/new-reactors/smr/licensing-activities/current-licensing-reviews/nuscale-us460.html) [BWXT BANR page](https://www.bwxt.com/sectors/nuclear-energy/smrs-microreactors/bwxt-advanced-nuclear-reactor-banr/)

NuScale remained the most obvious public comparable because it had advanced further within the NRC's established light-water architecture. The NRC page for the US460 described a 77 MWe light-water module, and the agency completed review activities for the US460 standard design approval in May 2025. But NuScale also carried the sector's most visible commercial scar: in November 2023 it and UAMPS agreed to terminate the Carbon Free Power Project after it became clear the project was unlikely to secure enough subscription to proceed. NuScale later shifted emphasis toward other commercial channels, including a nearly 2 GW data-centre arrangement with Standard Power. That left the company with a genuine regulatory asset but a damaged case study in first-project bankability. [NuScale US460 NRC page](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/new-reactors/smr/licensing-activities/current-licensing-reviews/nuscale-us460.html) [NuScale/UAMPS CFPP termination](https://www.nuscalepower.com/press-releases/2023/utah-associated-municipal-power-systems-and-nuscale-power-agree-to-terminate-the-carbon-free-power-project) [NuScale-Standard Power announcement](https://www.nuscalepower.com/press-releases/2023/standard-power-chooses-nuscales-approved-smr-technology-and-entra1-energy-to-energize-data-centers)

BWXT, by contrast, was not trying to persuade the market that its entire corporate future rested on the first commercial customer for a novel reactor. Its BANR microreactor programme was a transportable, TRISO-fuelled high-temperature gas reactor designed for 75 MW thermal output, and BWXT's Project Pele work gave it a direct path through the Department of Defense. Yet its investment case remained anchored in a much larger naval and government-nuclear franchise. That meant less pure upside to a speculative AI-power rerating than Oklo, but also far less binary balance-sheet dependence on one licensing and construction sequence. [BWXT BANR page](https://www.bwxt.com/sectors/nuclear-energy/smrs-microreactors/bwxt-advanced-nuclear-reactor-banr/) [BWXT Project Pele announcement](https://www.bwxt.com/bwxt-to-build-first-advanced-microreactor-in-united-states/)

## Private Developers: Different Technologies, Different End Markets

The private field was broader and, in several cases, better funded. X-energy was advancing the Xe-100 high-temperature gas-cooled reactor under DOE's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program, and in March 2023 Dow and X-energy signed a joint development agreement for a four-unit Xe-100 facility at a Dow Gulf Coast site. X-energy and Energy Northwest later signed a joint development agreement for up to 12 Xe-100 units, or 960 MW, in Washington. The commercial signal there differed from Oklo's: larger modules, industrial heat adjacency and a TRISO-fuel supply chain rather than a behind-the-meter fast-reactor electricity play. [Dow-X-energy JDA](https://x-energy.com/media/news-releases/dow-and-x-energy-advance-efforts-to-deploy-first-advanced-small-modular-nuclear-reactor-at-industrial-site-under-does-advanced-reactor-demonstration-program) [Energy Northwest-X-energy JDA](https://x-energy.com/media/news-releases/energy-northwest-x-energy-joint-development-agreement-xe-100)

TerraPower remained the closest private analogue in terms of fast-spectrum ambition, but not in scale or operating model. The Natrium design paired a roughly 345 MWe sodium-cooled reactor with molten-salt storage capable of boosting output to about 500 MWe during peak demand. Construction on the non-nuclear portion of the Kemmerer project began in June 2024, and TerraPower received a pivotal Wyoming siting permit in January 2025. That was a different proposition from Aurora: larger units, storage-assisted grid-scale dispatch, and a much more utility-shaped project footprint. [TerraPower groundbreaking release](https://www.terrapower.com/downloads/grounbreaking-press-release.pdf) [TerraPower permit release](https://www.terrapower.com/terrapower-awarded-pivotal-state-permit-for-natrium-plant) [TerraPower FAQ](https://www.terrapower.com/faq/)

Kairos Power occupied still another lane. The NRC approved a construction permit for the Hermes demonstration reactor in December 2023, making it one of the most tangible advanced-reactor licensing successes of the period. Kairos's fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature architecture, however, sat in a different technological family from Oklo's metallic-fuel sodium fast reactor. The competitive relevance lay less in direct module-to-module substitution than in whether Kairos could create regulatory precedent and industrial confidence for non-light-water systems generally. [Kairos Hermes permit announcement](https://www.kairospower.com/updates/nuclear-regulatory-commission-approves-construction-permit-for-hermes-demonstration-reactor)

GE Hitachi and Westinghouse represented the more conventional end of the SMR spectrum. Ontario Power Generation received a Canadian licence to construct one BWRX-300 at Darlington on 4 April 2025, while Westinghouse launched the AP300 in May 2023 as a 300 MWe derivative of the operating AP1000 fleet. Both designs benefited from the familiarity of light-water technology and more orthodox utility deployment models, even if their first-of-a-kind economics still required proof. [OPG Darlington SMR page](https://www.opg.com/powering-ontario/our-generation/nuclear/darlington-nuclear/darlington-new-nuclear/) [Westinghouse AP300 launch](https://info.westinghousenuclear.com/news/westinghouse-launches-ap300-smr)

## Oklo's Actual Differentiators

Oklo's differentiation rested on three claims that were real, even if none was self-executing.

| Developer | Technology | Module size | Fuel basis | Commercial model | Status inside frozen window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Oklo | Sodium fast reactor | 15-75 MWe | HALEU, with recycled/down-blended pathway | Build-own-operate PPA model | DOE pilot pathway plus NRC topical work |
| NuScale | Light-water SMR | 77 MWe per module | LEU | Technology and project-development model | NRC US460 review completed; CFPP terminated |
| X-energy | HTGR | 80 MWe per unit | TRISO/HALEU-adjacent fuel system | Reactor deployment with industrial partners | ARDP-backed project work with Dow, Energy Northwest |
| TerraPower | Sodium fast + storage | ~345 MWe core / ~500 MWe dispatch | HALEU-based | Utility-scale developer model | Kemmerer non-nuclear construction under way |
| Kairos | Fluoride-salt-cooled reactor | Demonstration pathway first | TRISO-based | Iterative demonstration path | Hermes construction permit issued |
| GE Hitachi | BWRX-300 light-water SMR | 300 MWe | LEU | Utility reactor supply | Darlington construction licence issued |
| Westinghouse | AP300 light-water SMR | 300 MWe | LEU | Utility reactor supply | AP300 launched; pre-licensing engagement |
| BWXT | HTGR / microreactor | 75 MWt BANR; Pele prototype smaller | TRISO | Contractor-led programme | Defence and microreactor development |

First, size. Oklo's own filings described the Aurora product line as designed to produce from 15 and up to 75 megawatts of electricity. That put Aurora well below the 300 MWe light-water programmes and even below NuScale's 77 MWe module. The smaller unit size opened customer categories that were not natural homes for utility-scale SMRs: remote bases, oilfield loads, individual data-centre campuses, and industrial sites that wanted tens rather than hundreds of megawatts. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

Second, business model. Oklo repeatedly told investors it intended to own and operate powerhouses itself, selling electricity and heat under long-term PPAs rather than primarily selling reactor equipment. That was not just a financing preference. It was the core of the claim that Oklo looked more like a future independent power producer than a nuclear OEM. Competitors such as NuScale, GE Hitachi and Westinghouse were structurally closer to technology licensors, project developers or equipment suppliers. [Oklo 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828025014490/oklo-20241231.htm) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

Third, customer positioning. Oklo's queue had become explicitly data-centre-facing earlier and more aggressively than most rivals. Equinix's paid 500 MWe optionality, Wyoming Hyperscale's 100 MW LOI, the two unnamed 750 MWe data-centre partnerships, Switch's 12 GW master agreement and Meta's 1.2 GW Ohio agreement gave Oklo a much denser AI-power narrative than utility-centric peers. [Oklo 2024 S-1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465924073383/oklo-20240331xs1.htm) [Wyoming Hyperscale announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Partners-with-Wyoming-Hyperscale-to-Deliver-100-Megawatts-to-its-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Switch master agreement announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx) [Oklo-Meta announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

## The Constraint Was Execution, Not Lack of Differentiation

Those distinctions did not erase the central competitive problem. By 23 May 2026, Oklo still had no operating plant, no binding customer PPA, and no commercial-scale domestic HALEU supply chain. Its regulatory path had also changed shape. The key question was no longer whether a resubmitted combined-licence application was already deep in NRC merits review; it was whether DOE's Reactor Pilot Program pathway for Aurora-INL, the March 2026 DOE Nuclear Safety Design Agreement, the May 2026 NRC principal-design-criteria approval and the company's stated intention to pursue subsequent NRC licensing could be converted into a bankable construction-and-operations sequence fast enough to keep counterparties engaged. [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo NRC PDC approval announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Approved-for-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

That left the competitive landscape in a more nuanced place than the pure-bull or pure-bear narrative allowed. Oklo was not undifferentiated; it had the clearest small-scale, owner-operator, AI-load story in the listed cohort. But it also carried a heavier dependence than many peers on aligning several things that still did not fully exist at commercial scale: metallic-fuel supply, DOE-to-NRC regulatory sequencing, and first-plant execution under its own balance sheet and operating model. The market premium, in other words, priced a niche that was real. Whether that niche would prove durable depended on whether Oklo could become the first company to turn that particular configuration of technology, financing and customer demand into working commercial infrastructure.

chapters.title: From 2022 NRC denial through SPAC, Equinix LOI, and ongoing licensing
chapters.body:
## The January 2022 denial and what it forced

The document that most clearly reset Oklo's trajectory arrived on 3 January 2022, when the Nuclear Regulatory Commission denied, without prejudice, the company's first combined licence application for Aurora at Idaho National Laboratory. The NRC said the application lacked sufficient information in areas including accident analysis and classification of safety-related structures, systems and components. It was not a finding that Aurora itself was inherently unsafe; it was a finding that the application as submitted was not complete enough for continued review. [NRC denial press release](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/news/2022/22-002.pdf) [NRC Aurora page](https://www.nrc.gov/reactors/new-reactors/large-lwr/col/aurora-oklo.html)

That denial shaped every later catalyst. It forced Oklo to move away from the easier investor shorthand that it was simply "waiting on the NRC" and toward a longer sequence of pre-application work, topical-report development, DOE engagement and, eventually, a hybrid DOE-and-NRC pathway for Aurora-INL. The rejection also made the company unusually legible as a test case in whether the US regulatory system could accommodate a non-light-water developer without demanding a light-water filing package in everything but name.

## July 2023: The merger announcement and the demand thesis

The most important financing and narrative catalyst came on 11 July 2023, when Oklo announced its merger with AltC Acquisition Corp. The transaction valued Oklo at a pre-money equity value of $850 million and was expected to provide up to $500 million of gross capital, subject to redemptions. The same announcement made the customer thesis unusually explicit. Oklo said it had signed a letter of intent with Equinix, and the investor materials used the data-centre load case to argue that abundant intelligence would require abundant firm power. [Oklo-AltC merger announcement](https://www.oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2023/Oklo-an-Advanced-Fission-Technology-Company-to-Go-Public-via-Merger-with-AltC-Acquisition-Corp/default.aspx) [Oklo investor presentation, July 2023](https://oklo.com/files/doc_presentation/Oklo-Investor-Presentation-July-2023_vFinal.pdf)

That pairing mattered. The SPAC did not merely capitalise a nuclear startup; it reframed Oklo as an AI-infrastructure equity before most listed power companies were being discussed in those terms. Sam Altman's role as chair reinforced the association.

## May 2024: Listing, cash and the start of public-quarterly scrutiny

The business combination closed on 9 May 2024, and Oklo began trading on the NYSE on 10 May 2024. The company said the combination delivered approximately $306 million in gross proceeds before expenses. That listing moved every subsequent development from venture-stage signalling into public-market scrutiny: customer letters of intent had to be evaluated against SEC risk disclosures, and regulatory milestones had to be reconciled with actual agency documents rather than investor-deck aspiration. [Oklo listing announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Inc.-Begins-Trading-on-the-New-York-Stock-Exchange/default.aspx)

The post-listing commercial sequence was fast enough to matter. Diamondback's 50 MW LOI had been announced in April 2024, Wyoming Hyperscale's 100 MW LOI followed in May, two unnamed data-centre partnerships for up to 750 MWe were announced in November, and Switch signed a non-binding 12 GW master agreement in December 2024. The cadence of those announcements became a catalyst class in its own right because it suggested that the Equinix agreement had not been a one-off anomaly. [Diamondback LOI announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Signs-LOI-to-Supply-50-Megawatts-of-Power-to-Diamondback-Energy/default.aspx) [Wyoming Hyperscale announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Partners-with-Wyoming-Hyperscale-to-Deliver-100-Megawatts-to-its-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [750 MWe data-center announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Secures-Partnerships-for-Up-to-750-Megawatts-of-Power-for-U.S.-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Switch master agreement announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx)

## April 2025: Altman left, and DeWitte took the chair

The governance catalyst that drew the most attention came on 22 April 2025, when Altman resigned as chair and director. The company said the decision was not due to any disagreement with Oklo. The succession path was often misstated in later commentary; the company's own proxy made it clear that Jacob DeWitte, not John Jansen, became chairman in April 2025. [Oklo 8-K, April 22 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000110465925037472/tm2512904d1_8k.htm) [Oklo 2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000184905626000023/a2025proxy.htm)

From the market's perspective, that was a test of whether the equity's AI-adjacent premium could survive without the most recognisable technology sponsor in the boardroom. The company answered less with rhetorical reassurance than with accelerated capital raising, broader customer announcements and a visibly more active federal project pathway.

## The real 2025-2026 regulatory sequence

The dossier's earlier framing of this period as an NRC combined-licence review under a finalised Part 53 regime did not survive the primary-source check. The actual sequence was more complicated and, in some respects, more favourable to Oklo than the stale wording implied.

On 17 July 2025, Oklo said the NRC had completed Phase 1 of a pre-application readiness assessment and had identified no significant gaps. On 13 August 2025, Oklo and Atomic Alchemy were selected for three projects under DOE's Reactor Pilot Program. On 22 September 2025, Oklo held a groundbreaking ceremony for Aurora-INL at Idaho National Laboratory under that DOE pilot framework. On 17 March 2026, Oklo announced DOE approval of the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement and the Other Transaction Agreement for Aurora-INL, and said the project was advancing under DOE's authorisation pathway with subsequent NRC licensing to support commercial operations. Then, on 6 May 2026, Oklo announced NRC approval of the principal design criteria topical report for Aurora-INL. [Oklo readiness assessment announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Advances-Licensing-with-Completion-of-NRC-Readiness-Assessment/default.aspx) [Oklo Reactor Pilot Program selection](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selected-for-Three-Projects-Under-U-S--Department-of-Energys-Reactor-Pilot-Program/default.aspx) [Oklo groundbreaking announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Breaks-Ground-on-First-Aurora-Powerhouse/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo NRC PDC approval announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Approved-for-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx)

Part 53 itself was also later than some summaries suggested. The NRC's final rule for the risk-informed, technology-inclusive framework for advanced reactors was published in the Federal Register on 30 March 2026 and became effective on 29 April 2026. It was therefore not a May 2024 catalyst, nor was it the basis for an already-running NRC merits review by the frozen date. [Federal Register final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/03/30/2026-06048/risk-informed-technology-inclusive-regulatory-framework-for-advanced-reactors) [Federal Register correction notice](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-07090.pdf)

## What the catalysts actually were by 23 May 2026

By the frozen-window date, the operative catalyst set was therefore not "an NRC decision on a resubmitted COLA that was already under review." It was a sequence of DOE authorisation steps, NRC topical-report progress, continued capital raises, and attempts to convert non-binding customer demand into project-specific agreements. The next meaningful questions were whether DOE pilot execution could keep pace with the commercial queue, whether the company could translate PDC progress into a fuller licensing package, and whether the balance-sheet expansion from the 2025 and early-2026 equity issuances could close enough of the funding gap to make counterparties stay patient. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## Specialist commentary framing

No primary-source corporate, exchange, agency or court material within the frozen window surfaced any Aleabit-specific framing of Oklo.

The primary-source record did, however, make the real analytical fault line plain. Official filings and company releases showed a business that had assembled a large commercial queue and repeatedly refreshed its cash balance, while official NRC and DOE materials showed that the pathway to a revenue-producing plant still ran through novel regulatory sequencing and a constrained fuel supply chain. That tension, rather than any unsupported specialist note, was what actually governed the catalyst calendar.

chapters.title: Sodium-fast reactor IP, HALEU fuel cycle, and NRC Part 53 licensing
chapters.body:
## A reactor born in the Idaho desert

Aurora's intellectual and engineering lineage ran back to the Experimental Breeder Reactor II at Idaho National Laboratory, the sodium-cooled fast reactor that operated from 1964 to 1994. DOE's own summary of the programme highlighted the 1986 passive-safety tests in which operators disabled both normal and emergency shutdown systems and cut power to the primary coolant pumps; the reactor shut itself down through its own physics response. Oklo's commercial thesis did not consist of copying EBR-II outright, but of translating that design heritage into a much smaller factory-oriented product that could be deployed under a different commercial model. [DOE EBR-II overview](https://www.energy.gov/ne/articles/5-fast-facts-about-experimental-breeder-reactor-ii) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

That lineage mattered for more than branding. It gave Oklo a pre-existing body of fuel, materials and operational history to point to when explaining why a sodium fast reactor could claim passive shutdown behaviour without leaning on the massive concrete-and-water architecture of conventional light-water plants. It also explains why Idaho kept appearing in the company's story: the site, the legacy data, and the recovered EBR-II fuel were all part of the same inheritance.

## The Aurora architecture

Oklo's own disclosures showed that the company's public description of Aurora evolved as the product line broadened. In the June 2024 quarter, it still described the first commercial Aurora powerhouse as designed to produce up to 15 MWe. By the 2025 annual report, the formulation had widened: the Aurora product line was designed to produce from 15 and up to 75 megawatts of electricity on fresh, recycled or down-blended nuclear fuel. Earlier dossier language that described 15, 50 and 75 as thermal outputs was therefore incorrect; these were electric-output configurations in the company's own materials. [Oklo Q1 2024 financial statements](https://oklo.com/files/doc_financials/2024/q1/oklo-q1-2024-financial-statements-filed-5-13-2024.pdf) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

The architecture remained consistent across those configurations. Aurora was a sodium-cooled fast reactor using metallic fuel. It was designed to operate at low pressure relative to pressurised-water systems, to exploit the favourable heat-transfer properties of liquid sodium, and to preserve a hard neutron spectrum by avoiding a moderator. That combination was central to both the safety and the commercial claims: low pressure reduced one class of conventional reactor accident scenario, while fast-spectrum operation and metallic fuel supported the longer-run ambition to use recycled and down-blended fuels.

## HALEU, recycling and the real R&D edge

Aurora's fuel requirements put it in a much more specialised category than light-water SMRs. DOE defines HALEU as uranium enriched above 5% and below 20% uranium-235, and Oklo's filings repeatedly said the company expected to use fresh, recycled or down-blended nuclear fuel within that advanced-fuel envelope. That was not a mere procurement detail; it was one of the main reasons the company's research programme encompassed both power plants and fuel infrastructure. [DOE HALEU overview](https://www.energy.gov/ne/nuclear-reactor-technologies/advanced-reactor-technologies/high-assay-low-enriched-uranium-haleu) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

Oklo's R&D programme therefore extended beyond reactor-core design. The company had received recovered EBR-II fuel material from DOE in 2019, completed an end-to-end demonstration of an advanced fuel-recycling process in July 2024, and pursued DOE approvals for its Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility at Idaho National Laboratory. By March 2026, Oklo said DOE had approved the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement for the Aurora powerhouse at INL and that DOE Idaho had already approved the fuel-fabrication facility's NSDA in November 2025 and its preliminary documented safety analysis in December 2025. The research-fill point that earlier versions missed was that the "recycled fuel" ambition had not remained a vague founding myth; it had translated into concrete DOE-stage fuel-facility work inside the frozen window. [Oklo recycling demonstration announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-Completes-Successful-End-to-End-Demonstration-of-Advanced-Fuel-Recycling-Process/default.aspx) [Oklo fuel-fabrication PDSA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approves-Preliminary-Documented-Safety-Analysis-of-Oklos-Aurora-Fuel-Fabrication-Facility-as-Assembly-Begins-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx)

## Intellectual property: broader than a single patent family

Oklo's SEC disclosures were less grandiose about intellectual property than some secondary write-ups. The company said it protected its IP through patents, trademarks, domain names, copyrights and trade secrets; held US patents and pending applications in several jurisdictions; and acquired patents and technology licences when advantageous. It also said, notably, that no single patent, licence or related group of patents or licences was critical or essential to the business as a whole. That is a more grounded description of the moat than language implying that one proprietary fuel recipe or one reactor-vessel claim was doing the defensive work alone. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

The implication was that Oklo's defensibility lay in a bundle: design know-how drawn from fast-reactor experience, access to DOE relationships and data, accumulated fuel-development work, site-specific safety documentation, and a conventional portfolio of patents and trade secrets around planned areas of development. In an advanced-nuclear setting, that bundle may matter more than any individual claim on paper because regulators, customers and constructors care about integrated execution, not just formal patent boundaries.

## Licensing and the regulatory R&D loop

The licensing story was also more iterative than earlier versions suggested. Oklo submitted its initial custom combined licence application in March 2020. The NRC denied it without prejudice in January 2022. In the June 2024 quarter, Oklo still said it was working toward an updated COLA for review. But the next two years did not resolve into a simple resubmission under a ready-made Part 53 framework. The NRC completed a Phase 1 readiness assessment in July 2025; DOE selected Aurora-INL for the Reactor Pilot Program in August 2025; DOE later approved the Aurora-INL NSDA in March 2026; and the NRC approved the principal design criteria topical report in May 2026. [Oklo Q2 2024 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000141057824001386/oklo-20240630x10q.htm) [Oklo readiness assessment announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Advances-Licensing-with-Completion-of-NRC-Readiness-Assessment/default.aspx) [Oklo Reactor Pilot Program selection](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selected-for-Three-Projects-Under-U-S--Department-of-Energys-Reactor-Pilot-Program/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo NRC PDC approval announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Approved-for-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx)

Part 53 itself arrived late in the window, not early. The NRC's final rule on the risk-informed, technology-inclusive framework for advanced reactors was published on 30 March 2026 and became effective on 29 April 2026. That made it a live backdrop for future licensing strategy, but not the regulatory framework under which Aurora was already deep into a formal merits review by May 2024 or even by most of 2025. [Federal Register final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/03/30/2026-06048/risk-informed-technology-inclusive-regulatory-framework-for-advanced-reactors) [Federal Register correction notice](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-07090.pdf)

## What the R&D base really amounted to

By the frozen-window date, Oklo's technical edge still had to be described carefully. The company had not yet proved Aurora in commercial operation. It had, however, advanced beyond aspirational renderings. The record showed inherited fast-reactor data, DOE-backed fuel work, an enlarging product range from 15 to 75 MWe, formal IP protections that extended across multiple technology areas, and a licensing programme that had resumed movement after the 2022 setback through both NRC and DOE channels. That was not proof that the R&D would convert cleanly into a fleet business. It was proof that the engineering and fuel-development base was deeper, and more institutionally embedded, than a casual reading of the ticker might suggest.

chapters.title: NRC licensing, HALEU supply, LOI-to-revenue conversion, capital raise need
chapters.body:
## The Five-Layer Risk Stack

Five dependencies still had to align before Oklo could collect durable reactor revenue: regulatory authorisation, fuel availability, customer conversion, construction execution and capital sufficiency. Those risks were not unique to Oklo, but the company's business model concentrated them unusually tightly. A utility buying a more conventional reactor could spread responsibility across vendors, fuel suppliers, regulators and operating entities. Oklo intended to carry much more of that chain itself. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

## Regulatory authorisation: no longer a simple "COLA under review" story

The foundational risk remained regulatory, but the correct risk framing was not that a resubmitted combined-licence application was already moving through a conventional NRC merits review. Oklo's first Aurora application was denied without prejudice in January 2022 because the NRC found that the filing lacked sufficient information. In the June 2024 quarter, Oklo said it was working toward an updated COLA. By July 2025 the company said the NRC had completed a Phase 1 readiness assessment with no significant gaps identified. By March 2026, however, Oklo had also moved onto DOE's Reactor Pilot Program pathway for Aurora-INL and said it would subsequently pursue NRC licensing to support commercial operations. [NRC denial press release](https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/news/2022/22-002.pdf) [Oklo Q2 2024 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000141057824001386/oklo-20240630x10q.htm) [Oklo readiness assessment announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Advances-Licensing-with-Completion-of-NRC-Readiness-Assessment/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx)

That sequencing created both an opportunity and a new uncertainty. The opportunity was that DOE authority could accelerate an early project at INL relative to a pure NRC-only route. The uncertainty was that this was still not a mature, repeated commercial pattern. Oklo was trying to bridge DOE pilot authorisation, NRC topical-report work, and later NRC commercial licensing into one coherent development path. Any slippage or mismatch among those channels could reverberate through customer schedules and financing plans.

Part 53 did not remove that uncertainty inside the frozen window. The NRC's final rule for the risk-informed, technology-inclusive framework for advanced reactors was published only on 30 March 2026 and became effective on 29 April 2026. That made it too late to serve as the already-settled basis for most of Oklo's earlier project calendar. [Federal Register final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/03/30/2026-06048/risk-informed-technology-inclusive-regulatory-framework-for-advanced-reactors) [Federal Register correction notice](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-07090.pdf)

## Fuel: HALEU was still the structural chokepoint

Aurora required HALEU, and that fuel remained the single clearest industrial bottleneck. DOE defines HALEU as uranium enriched above 5% and below 20% U-235. The United States had begun trying to rebuild domestic supply, but the timing gap remained large. Congress enacted the Russian uranium import ban in May 2024; DOE later announced up to $2.7 billion in enrichment awards; Centrus said in June 2025 that it had delivered 900 kilograms of HALEU to DOE. Those were real milestones, but they did not amount to an industrial-scale supply chain for dozens or hundreds of Aurora deployments. [DOE HALEU overview](https://www.energy.gov/ne/nuclear-reactor-technologies/advanced-reactor-technologies/high-assay-low-enriched-uranium-haleu) [Congress.gov: H.R. 1042](https://www.congress.gov/index.php/bill/118th-congress/house-bill/1042) [DOE enrichment awards announcement](https://www.energy.gov/articles/doe-announces-27-billion-president-bidens-investing-america-agenda-boost-domestic-nuclear) [Centrus 900 kg milestone](https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/centrus-achieves-key-production-milestone-with-delivery-of-900-kilograms-of-haleu-to-the-department-of-energy/)

Oklo's mitigants were meaningful but incomplete. It had an MOU with Centrus, had been awarded recovered EBR-II fuel material by DOE, and had advanced the Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility at INL through DOE safety approvals. But the company's own long-range customer queue implied fuel demand far beyond what had yet been demonstrated domestically. [Oklo-Centrus announcement](https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/oklo-and-centrus-energy-sign-memorandum-of-understanding-for-fuel-components-and-power-procurement-to-support-the-deployment-of-advanced-fission-technologies-in-southern-ohio/) [Oklo fuel-fabrication PDSA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approves-Preliminary-Documented-Safety-Analysis-of-Oklos-Aurora-Fuel-Fabrication-Facility-as-Assembly-Begins-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx)

## LOI conversion: credible demand, limited legal commitment

The customer book reduced demand risk, but it did not eliminate contract-conversion risk. Equinix had paid for queue position; Switch had signed a 12 GW framework; Diamondback, Wyoming Hyperscale and Meta had each supplied strategically useful commercial validation. Yet Oklo's 2025 annual report still said the company had not entered into any binding power purchase agreement with any customer to operate a plant or deliver electricity or heat. The risk was therefore not that customers were fictional. It was that customers' willingness to wait was finite, while licensing and construction risk remained open-ended. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Switch master agreement announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2024/Oklo-and-Switch-Form-Landmark-Strategic-Relationship-to-Deploy-12-Gigawatts-of-Advanced-Nuclear-Power-One-of-the-Largest-Corporate-Clean-Power-Agreements-Ever-Signed/default.aspx) [Oklo-Meta announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

For a pre-revenue nuclear developer, time itself was a commercial risk. A non-binding customer can be strategically important in year one and commercially irrelevant in year four if the customer's own load-growth, financing or grid options change. Oklo had reduced the question of whether anyone wanted the product. It had not eliminated the question of whether those same customers would sign and fund projects on Oklo's eventual timetable.

## Construction execution: first-of-a-kind remained first-of-a-kind

Aurora-INL also remained a first plant. That fact did not disappear because Kiewit had been selected as lead constructor or because groundwork had begun at INL. Oklo's scale advantage was real: a 15-to-75 MWe plant should be physically simpler than a gigawatt-scale nuclear unit, and the company repeatedly presented Aurora as a manufactured product rather than a bespoke megaproject. But the United States had little recent evidence that first-of-a-kind reactor deployments, even smaller ones, could avoid schedule friction, procurement surprises, scope changes and regulatory spillovers. [Oklo-Kiewit announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selects-Kiewit-as-the-Lead-Constructor-for-First-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx) [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm)

The more subtle risk was that Oklo's owner-operator model internalised mistakes that an equipment vendor might otherwise externalise. If the plant ran late, cost too much, or underperformed, the company would not merely lose a sales margin; it could impair the economics of the whole power-purchase model and weaken the next customer negotiation.

## Capital: bigger balance sheet, same structural need

Capital risk became less immediate and more strategic as the share price rose. By 31 March 2026, Oklo held roughly $2.537 billion of cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities after successive equity raises. That was a far stronger position than the company had at the May 2024 listing or even at year-end 2024. But the existence of cash did not settle the total funding need for first-plant completion and fleet buildout, because the company also intended to own plants, finance construction and carry fuel and operating risk on its own platform. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

The filings' liquidity language remained conservative. Even after the enlarged cash position, management continued to state that existing liquidity was expected to be sufficient for at least one year from issuance of the financial statements. That was prudent disclosure, but it also underscored that the balance sheet was a bridge through development, not proof that the entire build-own-operate journey had been financed on terms already locked in. [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## The compound probability

The most serious risk to the Oklo thesis was not any single item above. It was the requirement that all five gates clear in sequence, with only limited room for error at any stage. DOE and NRC authorisation had to progress coherently. Fuel supply had to move from pilot-scale to deployable. Non-binding customers had to become binding customers. A first plant had to be built and run. Capital had to remain available on acceptable terms through all of that. Oklo had assembled better inputs than many advanced-reactor peers: a deep cash balance, a visible customer queue, DOE site access, EBR-II fuel heritage and a clear commercial niche in smaller behind-the-meter load. None of those strengths removed the arithmetic of sequential risk. They only made the option worth underwriting in the first place.

chapters.title: NRC milestones, Aurora-INL construction, and the 2026-2030 horizon
chapters.body:
## The regulatory crucible

The central forward-looking question as of 23 May 2026 was no longer whether the NRC was quietly counting down to a decision on a resubmitted combined-licence application already under review. The primary-source record pointed to a different sequence. Oklo had completed an NRC Phase 1 readiness assessment in July 2025; Aurora-INL had been selected for DOE's Reactor Pilot Program in August 2025; the company had broken ground at Idaho National Laboratory in September 2025; DOE had approved the Nuclear Safety Design Agreement and associated Other Transaction Agreement for Aurora-INL in March 2026; and the NRC had approved the principal design criteria topical report in May 2026. Oklo said Aurora-INL was advancing under DOE's authorisation pathway and that it would subsequently pursue NRC licensing to support commercial operations. [Oklo readiness assessment announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Advances-Licensing-with-Completion-of-NRC-Readiness-Assessment/default.aspx) [Oklo Reactor Pilot Program selection](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selected-for-Three-Projects-Under-U-S--Department-of-Energys-Reactor-Pilot-Program/default.aspx) [Oklo groundbreaking announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Breaks-Ground-on-First-Aurora-Powerhouse/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx) [Oklo NRC PDC approval announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklos-NRC-Principal-Design-Criteria-Topical-Report-Approved-for-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx)

That means the earlier dossier phrasing that "no binding NRC decision date had been publicly disclosed" required refinement rather than mere repetition. There was indeed no disclosed NRC merits-decision date running inside the frozen window, but the reason was not simply opacity. It was that the lead project had shifted into a DOE pilot authorisation lane, with later NRC licensing still to come. The forward calendar was therefore governed by DOE pilot execution, follow-on licensing preparation and project delivery discipline, not by one published NRC hearing date.

## Part 53: later, and less immediately determinative, than advertised

Part 53 also mattered differently than the earlier draft suggested. The NRC's final rule for the risk-informed, technology-inclusive framework for advanced reactors was published in the Federal Register on 30 March 2026 and became effective on 29 April 2026. It was not final at the May 2024 SPAC close, nor was it the settled basis of a live Aurora merits review through most of 2025. As of the frozen date it had become part of the regulatory backdrop, but not a magic accelerant that had already de-risked the schedule. [Federal Register final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/03/30/2026-06048/risk-informed-technology-inclusive-regulatory-framework-for-advanced-reactors) [Federal Register correction notice](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-07090.pdf)

## Aurora-INL: from siting story to build sequence

The operational outlook had, however, become more concrete than it was immediately after the SPAC close. Oklo's July 2025 announcement naming Kiewit as lead constructor said pre-construction was expected to begin in 2025 and commercial operations were targeted for late 2027 to early 2028. The September 2025 groundbreaking and the March 2026 DOE NSDA approval showed that Aurora-INL had moved from being a notional first plant to being an actual build programme under federal oversight. [Oklo-Kiewit announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Selects-Kiewit-as-the-Lead-Constructor-for-First-Aurora-Powerhouse-in-Idaho/default.aspx) [Oklo groundbreaking announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/Oklo-Breaks-Ground-on-First-Aurora-Powerhouse/default.aspx) [Oklo DOE NSDA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Announces-U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approval-for-Nuclear-Safety-Design-Agreement-of-Aurora-Powerhouse-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx)

That still left a wide execution gap. The company had not yet constructed an operating powerhouse, and the path from first groundwork to a functioning sodium fast reactor remained exposed to engineering, procurement, fuel and regulatory dependencies that had not yet been tested together in the United States under this business model.

## Fuel and fabrication: real progress, unresolved scale

The fuel outlook was mixed in the same way. Domestic HALEU supply was moving, but not yet abundant. DOE had backed enrichment expansion, Centrus had delivered 900 kilograms of HALEU to DOE by June 2025, and Oklo had advanced both Aurora-INL and the Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility through DOE safety-review steps. Those were meaningful advances compared with the position a year earlier. But none of them yet established a scaled, routine supply chain for a multi-project commercial rollout. [DOE enrichment awards announcement](https://www.energy.gov/articles/doe-announces-27-billion-president-bidens-investing-america-agenda-boost-domestic-nuclear) [Centrus 900 kg milestone](https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/centrus-achieves-key-production-milestone-with-delivery-of-900-kilograms-of-haleu-to-the-department-of-energy/) [Oklo fuel-fabrication PDSA announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2025/U-S--Department-of-Energy-Approves-Preliminary-Documented-Safety-Analysis-of-Oklos-Aurora-Fuel-Fabrication-Facility-as-Assembly-Begins-at-Idaho-National-Laboratory/default.aspx)

## Converting the queue

Commercially, the next stage was no longer about proving that there was interest in small-scale clean firm power for data centres and industrial load. Oklo had already shown that. The question had become whether the company could convert queue position into binding project agreements before customer patience ran out. The 2025 annual report still said Oklo had not entered into any binding power purchase agreement with a customer to operate a plant or deliver electricity or heat, even as the March 2026 10-Q said the company was negotiating term sheets and binding PPAs with customers that had previously signed non-binding agreements. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

The commercial queue was also no longer confined to one geography. The January 2026 Meta agreement in southern Ohio contemplated development that could scale to 1.2 GW, with Oklo saying the first phase was targeted to come online as early as 2030. That suggested the company was already trying to map a post-Aurora-INL rollout, even before the first flagship plant had begun operations. [Oklo-Meta announcement](https://oklo.com/newsroom/news-details/2026/Oklo-Meta-Announce-Agreement-in-Support-of-1-2-GW-Nuclear-Energy-Development-in-Southern-Ohio/)

## Capital requirements

The financial outlook was stronger than the older straight-burn narrative implied, but it was not settled. By 31 March 2026, Oklo held approximately $2.537 billion of cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities. That gave management room to fund development, procurement and organisational scale-up from a much stronger base than existed at the time of the May 2024 listing. Yet the company also said it expected significant expenditures related to the deployment of Aurora powerhouses, fuel fabrication, fuel recycling and isotope production. The balance sheet had bought time; it had not eliminated capital-intensity. [Oklo 2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001849056/000162828026018698/oklo-20251231.htm) [Oklo Q1 2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1849056/000162828026034095/oklo-20260331.htm)

## The central question

The outlook at the frozen date was therefore neither the simple bull case nor the simple bear case. Oklo had done more than stay alive: it had accumulated capital, broadened its customer queue, moved Aurora-INL into a DOE build pathway, advanced fuel-fabrication approvals and secured an NRC topical milestone. But it still had not crossed the threshold that matters most in this industry: commercial operation of a plant delivering power under a binding long-term arrangement. The near-term future depended on whether those many preparatory milestones would begin to collapse into one another rather than remain parallel promises.

That was the real outlook. The thesis had matured from "can this company get attention?" to "can it turn federal authorisation, specialised fuel work and a highly visible but mostly non-binding customer queue into a functioning first plant on a commercially relevant timetable?" As of 23 May 2026, the answer was still unresolved, but the question was better specified than it had been a year earlier.
